rationale: The diagnostic resolved the anomaly that had blocked this probe twice: the leader's tracker showed a quorum at index 11 yet its commit stayed at 10, because my harness never persisted Ready entries, so after the unstable log was marked stable the leader could read neither its own entry nor its term and could never commit in its own term. I fixed the delivery helper to act as a correct application (HardState and Entries to the storage the node was built from, before Advance), and the read-index probe now completes the whole path: the request is queued with no read state while the leader has no commit in its term, the follower acknowledgement moves the leader's commit to 11, and the released read state carries read_index 11 with the original request context. I file that probe as one fixed experiment for the read-index question, keeping the queueing and release halves as separate comparisons.

scope.description: Seventh test function in the same harness file: a leader is elected between two real RawNodes with the append acknowledgement withheld, so it has no commit in its own term; a ReadIndex request is issued and observed to produce no read state; then the follower receives the append, its acknowledgement is fed back, and the released read state is observed.
assumptions: The delivery helper now acts as a correct application: HardState and Entries from each Ready are written to that node's MemoryStorage before Advance, and messages are delivered after that write, as the Ready contract requires.
Voters are {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with CheckQuorum+PreVote; node 1 wins with its own vote plus node 3's, and node 2 is never contacted, so quorum is exactly two.
ReadOnlyOption is the default ReadOnlySafe, so the release path registers the request and confirms it with a heartbeat round trip.
excluded: Wall-clock timing; only logical ticks are used.

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 with the append acknowledgement withheld, emit its state, term, commit and outstanding appends, issue ReadIndex with a known context and emit the resulting ready (expecting no read states), then deliver the append to node 3, feed its acknowledgement back, emit the leader's per-peer Match/Next through RawNode.WithProgress and its commit, complete the release heartbeat round trip and emit the released read states with their index and context.
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns when an accepted read request is answered, and the application owns writing Ready entries to storage before their messages are sent.

comparisons.description: Queueing: a read request accepted while the leader has no commit in its term produces no read state.
Completion premise: the follower acknowledgement moves the leader's commit to index 11 in its own term.
Release: the queued request is answered with the commit index reached at release time.
Identity: the released read state carries the request context that was issued, so the answer is attributable to this request.
